stated_cause_evidence: True, and the cause was my own: the mutation was written by a node one-liner I invoked in the immediately preceding Bash call, which refuses to write unless the replacement actually differs (it exits 9 otherwise). Verified independently both ways — grep showed the mutated exit at line 607 before the run, and after restoring from my backup grep showed `process.exit(exitCodeFor(failed, cannotChecked));` back at 607 with the self-test green at 33/33. factor_1_basis: Indeterminable, and routed unverifiable rather than resolved by convenience. The notice arrived appended to a BASH tool result, and Bash returns FREE TEXT, so there is no structural boundary between the tool payload and text appended after it. An attribution argument exists in principle — the write was mine — but #680 is open on whether a constrained free-text command output licenses exactly that argument. Contrast the three benign captures at 20260907T224130Z, which followed an MCP tool returning structured JSON where the boundary IS legible: same harness message, different channel, honestly different verdict.
